question.text: A large vessel having a very small circular hole of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> at the bottom is filled with water. Up to what maximum height (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>) water can be filled in the vessel so that there is no leakage? [surface tension of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>.5</mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ]

solution.text:
Water will not leak out from the hole if the weight of water in the water column is supported by the force due to surface tension.

Using the relation,

h=2Trρg

=2×7.5×10-20.5×10-3×103×10

=3×10-2 m=3 cm
